observed-secret-control > lost-control-b.rootCause: Product-side. (1) startControlPoll schedules the secret-bearing stop at windowEnd = nominal poll start + 2000 ms, and revocation can land only a few ms after that start (late timer + request latency), so the designed headroom is ~1-18 ms. (2) The parent event loop that runs that timer is blocked by the production tree tracker: launcher.ts trackTree() runs spawnSync('ps -A') every 25 ms during an observed run; on this machine one call blocks 14.2-15.9 ms (604 processes). Controlled probe with the real dist createForkSpawner: setTimeout lateness without trackTree median 1.62 / p90 2.12 / max 12.9 ms; with trackTree median 6.78 / p90 26.53 / max 50.47 ms. The overrun (0.2-20 ms past the bound) matches that lateness.
observed-secret-control > lost-control-b.classification: not a test-side timing defect; not caused by 012A; not fixed (any test-side change would loosen the 2000 ms product bound)
observed-secret-control > lost-control-b.recommendation: @dev/@architect: make tree tracking non-blocking (async ps or a coarser interval off the timer-critical path) and/or give the secret-control stop an explicit scheduling margin under the 2000 ms bound. The synchronous 25 ms ps loop also blocks the runner's HTTP server about 60% of the time per active run, which is a performance concern beyond this test.
